title: kernel hint indexer and proactive warmup orchestrator
author: Maya Chen
description: Context and motivation: Long-running benchmarks for heterogeneous model mixes show large variance in cold-start tails due to non-deterministic kernel selection and uneven primer distribution across cohorts. This PR introduces two complementary components: (1) a lightweight kernel-hint indexer that computes and serves hot-kernel candidates per model/cohort based on recent telemetry; and (2) a proactive warmup orchestrator that uses the indexer to drive opportunistic kernel warmups in low-impact windows. Goals: reduce p95/p99 cold-tail latency, lower warmup overhead during production mixing runs, and provide telemetry hooks to quantify warmup efficacy. What this PR does: Adds an indexer service (Go) that ingests summarized kernel heatmaps and exposes a compact hint API; implements an orchestrator (Python) that schedules warmup jobs with cohort-aware pacing and sequence-length-aware priming; adds a warmup_metrics_exporter (Rust) to emit delta histograms and warmup attribution tags into our bench telemetry pipeline; wires the bench CI to execute a nightly warmup-effectiveness job; documents the new knobs in docs/bench/primer-guidelines.md. Checklist: - [x] Indexer ingestion and hint API implemented - [x] Orchestrator scheduling + backoff/pacing policy - [x] Telemetry tags and delta histograms added - [x] Integration tests for scheduling/time-based gating - [x] Bench CI job + dashboard wiring - [x] Docs updated Related work: builds on ENG-6121 (kvcache priming design) and ENG-7019 (kernel affinity experiments). Links: Linear ENG-7482, design notes https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-7482/kernel-hint-indexer-design. Performance expectations: nightly job should show a 10–30% reduction in p99 for cold cohorts in mixed-model runs; steady-state token cost should not increase by more than 1.5% when warmups are enabled. Rollout plan: land behind feature flag bench.enable_proactive_warmup; start with simulated runs on perf-canary; enable for low-traffic tenants in Dedicated; monitor warmup attribution metrics for two weeks before broader rollout. Implementation details: indexer persists a rolling 6-hour kernel-score window, compressed into a <200KB hint blob per model; orchestrator consults the hint blob and schedules at most one warmup per model per 10 minutes with exponential backoff if trials are ineffective; warmup jobs are sequence-length stratified to avoid priming only short sequences. Backwards compatibility: all components are opt-in; default is disabled. Operational notes: added a CI pipeline that runs a warmup-effectiveness check nightly and fails if p99 regresses >5% relative to previous baseline. TODOs post-merge: add historical heatmap visualization to observability-pack and refine hint decay half-life based on broader runs.

release_notes: Introduce kernel hint indexer and proactive warmup orchestrator: - Adds an opt-in indexer that summarizes hot kernels per model for targeted warmups - Adds an orchestrator to schedule sequence-aware warmups with pacing and backoff - Emits warmup attribution telemetry and delta histograms for bench reporting - Nightly CI job to track warmup effectiveness - Feature behind bench.enable_proactive_warmup flag; no default change in behavior
notes_for_ops: Observe warmup.attribution metrics and delta p95/p99 histograms after enabling; if warmup-induced token cost exceeds 2% for a cohort, disable via feature flag and open ENG ticket. Indexer has a configurable retention and hint-size limit in bench-configs/profiles/warmup-feature-flag.yaml.
